slot.brief: For ideal-gas free expansion against vacuum, ask q, w, ΔU and ΔH — pure first-law sign/concept check, no numbers.

stem: An ideal gas undergoes adiabatic free expansion against vacuum. Which set of changes is correct?

verdicts.working: Adiabatic free expansion has q=0 and w=0, so ΔU=0. For an ideal gas, U and H depend only on temperature; thus ΔH=0.

working:
$q=0$ (adiabatic), $w=0$ (expansion against vacuum).
First law: $\Delta U=q+w=0$.
For an ideal gas, $U$ and $H$ depend only on $T$.
Thus $\Delta T=0$ and $\Delta H=0$.
